newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria's Ramadan toll - 157 dead in 12 days.
newsitem.headline: Algeria's Ramadan toll - 157 dead in 12 days.

text.p: Two car bombs killed at least three people and wounded scores in a garrison town south of Algiers on Wednesday, residents said, hours after two other explosions hit the capital in a relentless guerrilla "Ramadan" bombing campaign.
Suspected Moslem guerrillas also killed five other civilians, including a 12-year-old boy and his father, in two additional attacks in villages near Algiers this week, the El Watan daily said.
Two car bombs killed at least seven people in Algiers on Tuesday and wounded 54 more.
The Moslem fundamentalist Armed Islamic Group had promised to step up attacks during the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan.
It began on January 10 and Algerian newspapers said before Tuesday's attacks that at least 150 people had since died and more than 170 been wounded.
Following is a list of the main violence in that period:
Jan 12
- Moslem guerrillas kill 14 villagers in Tabainat hamlet, in Blida province, 50 km (30 miles) south of Algiers.
-The same day they kidnap five girls and cut their throats in the neighbouring village of Haouch Englise.
Jan 14
- Nine bodies are found in Djebel Koukou in Algiers and Bab Ali village, near Algiers, according to Algerian newspapers.
Jan 16
- At least four guerrillas killed in a seven-hour gunbattle with security forces on the heights of Algiers's ancient Casbah. Residents say more than 10 guerrillas died. Authorities say nothing.
- Bomb explodes in a car market in Boufarik, 30 km (20 miles) south of Algiers killing 12 people and wounding scores, according to the authorities. Newspapers put the death toll at 14.
Jan 19
- Car bomb explodes on Algiers' Belouizdad street killing 21 people and wounding 60, according to the authorities. Newspapers say 42 people were killed.

- Moslem guerrillas kill 36 people in Sidi Abdelaziz village, in Medea province, 70 km (40 miles) south of Algiers, according to the authorities. Newspapers put the toll at 48, with one paper, El Watan, saying 49 died as they were kneeling at prayer in a mosque.
Jan 20
- Bomb explodes by school for girls in an Algiers suburb. No casualties.
Jan 21
- Car bomb explodes in Boulevard des Martyrs, killing six people and wounding 44. Five hours later another blast kills one person near a children's merry-go-round at Boulevard Khelifa Oulmane.
